name: one-time-pad.txt
desc:
I've been recently considering the complexity of other peoples approaches, and considering whether a more simple approach is still feasible, i.e. without hints from JS, without complex mathematical formulas.

In this investigation, I was trying to evaluate an encryption process similar to Vigenere cipher but using a lookup tableau (created using K1-K2-K3). In my process the whole encryption is rotated 90 degrees right.  Obviously, I don't know what the keyword is but conceptually using this process it may be possible to work backward until a keyword or key phrase is revealed. It isn't really the goal here however, to find this keyword. Rather I'm just evaluating the idea of using the original sculpture to act as a lookup tableau.  So, yes, in this approach, I am using the plain-text hints from JS, to validate my theory.

Looking at the original Kryptos tableau, we can see that the original dimensions of the tableau were 30(wide)x26(high).  Was this a hint by JS?

We can visually rotate the Kryptos structure, to see 26 alternative source alphabets, starting with 'kryptosabcdefghijlmnquvwxz', then 'ryptosabcdefghijlmnquvwxzk' and so on. 

In my process, I try to use each of these alphabets, one at a time, to encrypt the known plain text, to create the crypt text. 

1) Create a new lookup tableau from the K1-K2-K3, into a 26(high)x30(wide) or 26(high)x31(wide), adding additional '.' characters where 'yhar' is found, to make the square.  These '.' characters are really a placeholder for a word or a phrase inserted into the tableau, by JS.  I don't know what that word is yet, so I'll just use a full stop to represent it.

2) For each row in the lookup tableau, determine which letters in the alphabet are present in the lookup tableau.  I'll be using this later to find the crypt text characters.

3)  I tried each alphabet one at a time, considering whether each of the plain text letters could be encrypted into the crypt text, by seeing if the crypt text characters appear in the list of character found in each row. I tried to record possible keyword characters.  It seems that the 'best fit' plain text alphabet is the kryptos alphabet starting 'mnquvwxzkryptosabcdefghijl'.

It is interesting to me that the process is quite successful in finding most of the crypt text. Not all letters are found. Remembering that where the "." characters appear in the tableau, there may be letters which satisfy the crypt text letters which are missing.  There is also a missing 'z' character from the last row of the lookup tableau, which has me stumped.  We are told that the letter 'Z' decrypts back to the letter 'L' in clock.  In my lookup tableau, the last row is the 'L' row, as it is the last letter of the 'mnquvwxzkryptosabcdefghijl' alphabet.  We know however, that intentional spelling mistakes have been used in the past. Could this be evidence of another?

It does however seem, with the right source alphabet, that this is a positive approach, one which fits the original concept of being feasible without prior knowledge and one I'll be looking into further.
